Champion model version 1; 104,897 logged replay predictions joined with their labels.
**SYNTHETIC REPLAY**: the monitored engines are the NASA test engines re-delivered batch by batch; their labels

## Reading the signals

Inputs drift as the replayed fleet ages: early windows hold only young, healthy engines, late windows only the few
long-lived engines close to failure. That shift is real but is not the model being wrong, which is why drift alone
only warns. Performance is compared within true-RUL bands so that a change in the mix of healthy and degraded engines
does not read as degradation.

Within a band, the replay still confounds age: all engines started together, so each window holds one age group.
The >125 band of windows 4-9 contains only engines that are already old yet far from failure (the long-lived ones),
which the model, using age, predicts conservatively. Their errors exceed the baseline by up to 75% in those windows,
while the same band over the whole replay is within tolerance. A real fleet mixes ages in every time slice; here the
retraining signal is therefore judged over the whole period (`monitoring.performance_scope`), and the per-window
cells are kept as diagnostics. An earlier run with per-window judgement fired, retrained a challenger (version 2,
same CV metric) and correctly did not promote it.
